claim: A defendant's continued detention after the completion of a traffic stop and subsequent probable cause vehicle search does not constitute an illegal seizure, even when the detention is prolonged beyond what was reasonably necessary to accomplish the purposes of the stop.
initial_reasoning: In State v. Smith, 209 N.E.3d 830 (Ill. 2007), the Illinois Supreme Court held that a police officer’s detention of a driver after a traffic stop and a subsequent vehicle search does not constitute an illegal seizure, even when the detention is prolonged beyond what was reasonably necessary to accomplish the purposes of the stop. This directly supports the claim.
